expectations.text: Scores candidates on the six named criteria: audience fit, audience size, brand alignment, engagement quality, reciprocity potential, and ease of execution
expectations.evidence: Table columns Fit, Size, Brand, Engagement, Reciprocity, Ease.

expectations.text: Ranks audience fit ahead of audience size, stating that fit filters and size ranks
Downgrades or rejects Tech Weekly Digest on audience fit despite its 54,000 subscribers
expectations.evidence: Fit 1; 'don't sign as a partner'; 'general tech newsletter fails fit for a Rust conference even at 50k subscribers.'

expectations.text: Downgrades or rejects the regional news site on audience fit because its readership is recruiters and CTOs rather than the event's target attendee
expectations.evidence: 'Recruiters and CTOs are not your attendees.' Fit 2, don't sign.

expectations.text: Rates Borrow Checker highly on fit and engagement despite it being the smallest list at 3,100 subscribers
expectations.evidence: Fit 5, Engagement 5; 'Its small size costs it points, but fit outranks size.'

expectations.text: Treats the Discord's roughly 400 monthly posters, not its 12,000 members, as the engagement-quality figure
expectations.evidence: '400 active posters out of 12,000 is about 3% monthly activity... the other 97% of members are mostly passive.' Engagement 2.

expectations.text: Applies an accept rule of fit plus at least one of size or engagement, rather than accepting on a summed or averaged total across all six criteria
expectations.evidence: 'The accept rule is fit plus at least one of size or engagement... The other criteria set the format, not the accept or reject call.'

expectations.text: Labels the scores as judgement that rank candidates against each other rather than certifying any of them
expectations.evidence: 'All scores are my own 1-5 judgement. They rank these five against each other and don't certify any of them.'
